jobs.description:
**About the job**

Help some of the world's largest enterprises get real value from AI. You'll grow a book of Whatfix's enterprise customers by bringing them new use cases, new applications and our AI-first products.

**Why this role**

* **Expansion-focused:** you won't carry renewals, so your time goes into growing accounts.
* **Existing & New AI products to sell:** into customers who already trust Whatfix.
* **Direct access to leadership:** work closely with our Co-Founder and CEO and our Global Head of Sales.
* **Uncapped incentives:** your upside grows with your accounts.

**About Whatfix**

Whatfix is an AI platform that helps enterprises get full value from the software and AI tools they invest in. We call this userization: technology should adapt to the user, not the other way round.

Our proprietary AI engine, ScreenSense, understands what a user is trying to do in an application and why, and delivers guidance, knowledge and automation in the flow of work. It powers Digital Adoption, Product Analytics and Mirror (simulation-based training), and our AI-first products: Seek, an AI assistant that acts across applications, and Mirror 2.0 for Gen AI role simulation.

We serve **700+ enterprise customers**, including 80+ Fortune 500 companies such as UPS Supply Chain Solutions.

We have raised **~$270M**, most recently a $125M Series E led by Warburg Pincus with SoftBank Vision Fund 2, and have been named a Leader in Digital Adoption Platform (DAP) reports by Gartner, Forrester, IDC and Everest Group for 5+ years running. We have four main offices in the US (San Jose), India (Bangalore and Gurgaon) and the UK (London), plus smaller offices in Germany, Singapore and Australia.

**The role**

As an Enterprise Account Manager, you will own a book of Whatfix's enterprise customers in your region and grow them.

Your quota comes entirely from expansion within those accounts: new business units, new applications and our newer AI products.

You will be based in our San Jose office and work closely with your customers in person, alongside our Customer Success, Solutions Consulting, Marketing and our product teams.

Our sales leadership, including our Co-Founder and CEO and our Global Head of Sales, is hands-on with the team, so expect direct mentorship and a short path from idea to decision.

**What you'll do**

* Own a portfolio of enterprise accounts end to end: expansion, cross-sell and account planning. This role does not carry renewals.
* Build relationships across each account, from CIOs and IT leaders to HR, L&D, CRM and procurement owners, so you are never single-threaded.
* Run structured discovery that gets to business impact, then build and quantify the ROI case for expansion.
* Find and open new business units and use cases inside your accounts.
* Position our AI products (Seek, Mirror 2.0 and the AI agents across our platform) credibly with senior buyers, and help customers shape how they roll out AI to their people.
* Use AI tools in your own work every day: account research, call prep, mutual action plans and follow-ups.
* Forecast accurately and keep the CRM current.
* Bring what you hear from customers back to Product and Marketing.

**What you'll bring**

* A track record of carrying and beating a quota in B2B SaaS, with real experience growing existing enterprise accounts through upsell and cross-sell.
* Experience in long, multi-stakeholder sales cycles with enterprise buyers, not only short transactional deals.
* Discovery and value-selling skills: you ask good questions, listen to the answers, and tie what you sell to the customer's business outcomes.
* The habit of building your own pipeline, including finding new teams and use cases inside accounts you already manage.
* AI fluency: you use AI tools daily in your own selling, and you can hold a confident, honest conversation with a CIO about how their organization adopts AI.
* Executive presence, preparation, and the honesty to say "I don't know, I'll find out" when that is the right answer.
* Coachability and curiosity. You seek feedback, act on it, and learn new products quickly.
* Comfort in a lean, fast-moving team where you will roll up your sleeves.

We hire for trajectory, not just pedigree. If you have moved from mid-market into enterprise, or from customer success or renewals into a commercial number, and you are on a steep learning curve, we want to hear from you.

**Where and how we work**

* **Location:** San Jose, CA. You will be based in our San Jose office.
* **Work model:** our teams work in the office 4 days a week to collaborate, build community and stay connected. US teams start their day early to overlap with other time zones, which keeps evenings free.
* **Travel:** up to 50% of your time, visiting customers across North America.

**Perks and benefits (US)**

* Uncapped incentives and an equity plan
* Mac shop: work with the latest tech
* Medical, dental and vision, with Whatfix covering 80% of premiums
* HSA: $1,000 individual / $2,000 family
* Monthly cell phone stipend and daily UberEats lunches
* Learning and development benefits, team and company outings
* Relocation and sponsorship available

**Our culture**

Customer First | Empathy | Transparency | Fail Fast & Scale Fast | No Hierarchies | Deep Dive & Innovate | Trust as the Foundation | Do It as You Own It

**Job Overview**

San Francisco Housing Development Corporation (SFHDC) seeks an Assistant Project Manager to advance the development and preservation of affordable housing in San Francisco.

About SFHDC

Black community leaders, led by Geraldine Johnson, founded SFHDC in 1988 to counter the displacement that 1960s and 1970s redevelopment caused for African American residents and other communities of color. Our mission is to foster financial stability through the development of affordable housing, the facilitation of homeownership, and the economic empowerment and revitalization of Bayview Hunters Point, the Fillmore, and other San Francisco neighborhoods.

We carry out this mission through four core programs: Affordable Housing Development, Resident Services, Financial Empowerment, and Economic Development.

**Real Estate Development.** The department develops and preserves a diverse portfolio of affordable housing and maintains an active pipeline of new projects. The portfolio spans new construction, redevelopment, and preservation, including ownership and rental homes, a cooperative housing property, and properties converted under the federal Rental Assistance Demonstration (RAD) program.

About the role

The Assistant Project Manager works alongside a Project Manager to deliver multiple affordable housing developments, including new construction and the rehabilitation and preservation of existing properties. Most projects are financed with Low-Income Housing Tax Credits (LIHTC), a federal program that provides tax credits to investors in exchange for equity in affordable rental housing, together with other public and private funding sources.

This entry-level position is designed to develop future project managers. The successful candidate will gain experience across the full development process, take on increasing responsibility over time, and follow a defined path to Project Manager.

Key responsibilities

Under the direction of the Project Manager, the Assistant Project Manager will:

· **Prepare funding applications.** Help assemble applications to MOHCD, the California Tax Credit Allocation Committee, and other public and private sources. Gather site plans, budgets, and partner letters, draft narrative sections for review, and check each submission against funder requirements.

· **Maintain project trackers and records.** Own the permit and approvals tracker, from Planning Department review through Department of Building Inspection (DBI) permits, monitor status with City staff, and flag potential delays to the Project Manager. Keep project files, schedules, and correspondence current.

· **Process monthly payment requests.** Reconcile contractor invoices to the approved budget to prepare monthly payment requests to lenders and public funders, and track the documentation required for loan closings.

· **Track project risks.** Keep the project risk log, identify potential funding, compliance, budget, and schedule issues, such as unmet lender conditions, delayed permits, or cost overruns, and escalate them to the Project Manager with relevant documentation.

· **Coordinate partner and community meetings.** Join the Project Manager in meetings with co-developers, lenders, and investors, and at public hearings and community meetings. Prepare materials and updates, take notes, and track follow-up items.

· **Update budgets and financial models.** Keep project budgets current and, as skills develop, run scenario analyses in Excel-based financial models.

· **Participate in site visits.** Visit construction sites and existing properties to document conditions and progress.

· **Assist with project closeout.** Assemble closeout documentation and help transition completed buildings to operations, in coordination with SFHDC’s Resident Services team.

The Assistant Project Manager also contributes to special projects, including process and tool improvements, and performs other duties as assigned.

Qualifications

**Required**

· Bachelor’s degree.

· One to two years of project management experience, or equivalent experience managing deadlines, budgets, and multiple stakeholders.

· Strong written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to draft accurate correspondence, reports, and funding narratives, and to present information to internal and external stakeholders.

· Demonstrated organizational skills and attention to detail, with the ability to manage competing priorities across multiple projects.

· Proficiency in Microsoft Office (Excel, Word, Outlook) and Google Workspace (Gmail, Docs, Sheets, Drive).

· Commitment to affordable housing and community development.

· Valid California driver’s license, a reliable vehicle, and proof of auto insurance.

**Preferred**

· Experience with Excel financial modeling.

· Knowledge of automation technology, such as workflow automation, e-signature, or project management software.

· Proficiency with AI tools to research topics, prepare first drafts of narratives and correspondence, and analyze data.

· Coursework or experience in planning, real estate, construction, finance, or public policy.

· Knowledge of San Francisco neighborhoods, particularly Bayview Hunters Point and the Fillmore.

Schedule and work location

· Full-time, 35 hours per week (five 7-hour days).

· Hybrid: two days per week in the San Francisco office (94124); remaining days remote or at project sites.

· Occasional evening public hearings and community meetings.

· Periodic local travel to project sites within San Francisco in a personal vehicle; mileage is reimbursed.

Physical requirements

San Francisco Housing Development Corporation (SFHDC) seeks a Project Manager to lead the development and preservation of affordable housing in San Francisco and to supervise and develop junior real estate staff.

**ABOUT SFHDC**

Black community leaders, led by Geraldine Johnson, founded SFHDC in 1988 to counter the displacement that 1960s and 1970s redevelopment caused for African American residents and other communities of color. Our mission is to foster financial stability by developing affordable housing, facilitating homeownership, and empowering the economic revitalization of Bayview Hunters Point, the Fillmore, and other San Francisco neighborhoods.

We carry out this mission through four core programs: Affordable Housing Development, Resident Services, Financial Empowerment, and Economic Development.

**Real Estate Development.** The department develops and preserves a diverse portfolio of affordable housing and maintains an active pipeline of new projects. The portfolio spans new construction, redevelopment, and preservation, including ownership and rental homes, a cooperative housing property, and properties converted under the federal Rental Assistance Demonstration program.

**ABOUT THE ROLE**

The Project Manager leads two to four affordable housing developments at a time, from feasibility and financing through construction, closing, and transition to operations. Projects include new construction and rehabilitating and preserving existing properties. Most are financed with Low-Income Housing Tax Credits, combined with City, state, and private funding sources.

The Project Manager is accountable for each project's schedule, budget, and financing, and directs the work of architects, contractors, attorneys, and consultants. The Project Manager also supervises and coaches the Assistant Project Manager and real estate interns. This position reports to the Interim Director and offers a path to Senior Project Manager.

**KEY RESPONSIBILITIES**

· **Lead projects from start to finish.** Set the strategy, schedule, and budget for two to four projects and drive each one through feasibility, financing, construction, loan closing, and transition to operations with SFHDC's Resident Services team. Report monthly to the Interim Director and the Board on progress and risks.

· **Secure financing and negotiate the deal.** Lead applications to City and state housing funders, select lenders and investors, and negotiate term sheets, loan documents, and partnership agreements with legal counsel.

· **Own budgets, models, and contingency.** Build each project's development budget, operating budget, and Excel pro forma. Test scenarios such as higher interest rates or lower tax credit pricing, decide when to use contingency, and present options when a funding gap appears.

· **Lead approvals and represent SFHDC.** Manage Planning Department approvals, environmental review, and Department of Building Inspection permits. Present projects to City funders, the Planning Commission, and community meetings.

· **Build and manage the development team.** Select architects, general contractors, and consultants through requests for proposals, negotiate their contracts, and lead owner, architect, and contractor meetings. Monitor construction cost, schedule, and quality, and approve change orders and payment requests within delegated authority.

· **Supervise and coach the Assistant Project Manager.** Assign and review work, give regular feedback, conduct annual reviews, and prepare the Assistant Project Manager for promotion. Supervise real estate interns.

· **Plan the future of existing properties.** Assess older SFHDC properties, including Rental Assistance Demonstration and cooperative housing, for refinancing, rehabilitation, or recapitalization, and develop plans that keep homes affordable and in good condition.

· **Pursue new opportunities.** Evaluate sites, acquisitions, and City requests for proposals, and prepare feasibility analyses and go/no-go recommendations for the Interim Director.

The Project Manager also leads special projects, including process and tool improvements, and performs other assigned duties.

POSITION: Case Manager, Housing Retention Services

PROGRAM/LOCATION: Santa Clara County, Solaire Apts

SUPERVISOR: Program Manager

JOB TYPE: Full Time, Non-Exempt

COMPENSATION: $30.96/Hourly

**ABOUT HOMEFIRST**

Established in 1980, HomeFirst™ is a nonprofit organization passionately working to end homelessness. We serve the Bay Area community through low-barrier programming and systems leadership – meeting each person where they are by offering support and resources that address immediate and long-term housing needs. With 45 years of experience, we view housing as a fundamental human right and understand that solving homelessness requires a collaborative effort.

**POSITION OVERVIEW:**

A Housing Retention Case Manager is responsible for providing comprehensive support services to help individuals and families participating in permanent supportive housing programs. Their intensive and individualized case management services are coupled with linkage to a network of community resources to assist clients in averting homelessness, maintaining housing, and increasing self-sufficiency. To this end, the Housing Retention Case Manager participates in our collective effort to end and prevent homelessness.

**REPORTING RELATIONSHIPS**

The position reports to the Program Manager.

**PRIMARY RESPONSIBILITIES:**

Maintain a caseload of 20-30 participants.

Provide comprehensive case management services. This may include:

Initial eligibility verification and enrollment

Ongoing needs and status assessments

Budgeting

Administration of financial assistance

Information and referral

Crisis de-escalation

Safety planning, risk assessment, and mandated reporting

Employment and benefits assistance

Advocacy

Other direct service provision

Meet with participants at a frequency and location determined by their needs.

Engage in the consistent application of evidence-based practices.

Support internal program support specialist activities as needed. This may include:

Street-based or community outreach efforts

Landlord engagement

Workshop coordination

Participate in case conferencing and collaborative care coordination.

Maintain compliance with contract, agency, and licensing requirements.

Achieve identified program and position deliverables.

Adhere to task completion deadlines.

Maintain thorough and accurate documentation of participant services in accordance with agency and contractual standards.

Attend all job-related meetings, including program staff meetings and agency-wide meetings.

Participate in opportunities for learning and skill maintenance/development.

Utilize supervision appropriately, maintaining open lines of communication and providing updates on activity.

Assist with other duties as assigned.

**QUALITIES:**

The Housing Retention Services Case Manager is passionate about serving others and sees themself in a helping profession long term. They are pro-active and responsive to the needs of our participants, meeting them “where they’re at” and bridging the gap between the individual and our services. They manage their time well and demonstrate strong organizational abilities. With the support of program leadership, the Case Manager participates in our culture of learning and increases their knowledge of evidence-based practices over the course of their employment. Together, we model the values and principles of HomeFirst within the agency and broader community.

HomeFirst is a diverse company in a diverse field, and the Case Manager seeks to work with people from a variety of social and economic backgrounds. They are a highly collaborative member of our participant services team and enjoy a team-oriented work environment.

**BENEFITS**

HomeFirst provides comprehensive benefits, including 100% employer-paid medical, dental, and vision coverage and additional wellness options like chiropractic care, mental health support, pet insurance, and an Employee Assistance Program. We offer a 401(k)-retirement plan with generous matching, life and disability insurance, flexible spending accounts, commuter benefits, and workers’ compensation. Employees enjoy 12 holidays, sick leave, and PTO starting at 15 days annually, increasing with tenure, plus 4 hours of civic engagement leave annually to volunteer.

**ORGANIZATIONAL EQUITY STATEMENT**

At HomeFirst, diversity, equity, and inclusion guide our services, workplace, and decisions. Recognizing housing as a social justice issue, we prioritize equitable practices, honor lived experiences, and uphold dignity for all. By fostering belonging, accountability, and continuous improvement, we embed DEI values in our processes, recruitment, and leadership, striving for excellence at every level.

HomeFirst is proud to be an Equal Opportunity and Affirmative Action employer and considers qualified applicants for employment without regard to race, color, creed, religion, national origin, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, age, disability, veteran status, or any other status protected by law. **At Cynch, the client comes first.** We’re a full-service tax, accounting, and advisory firm serving small businesses and entrepreneurs. Our experienced professionals provide tax preparation, bookkeeping, payroll, planning, and advisory services while building lasting client relationships and solving complex financial problems.

Our proprietary AI platform reduces routine work, **giving our professionals more time to deliver deeper insights, smarter financial guidance, and personalized service**. It supports their expertise; our people remain accountable for the outcomes.

**We’re a growing practice with clear paths for career advancement.** We grow organically and through strategic acquisitions, creating new opportunities for our team. Each level has defined expectations and advancement criteria, with a performance-based path to greater responsibility and equity over time.

**We are looking for a Project Manager for Practice Operations.** Reporting to the Managing Director and supporting the executive team, you'll own the practice's cross-functional projects from start to finish. You'll scope the work, set owners and milestones, track progress, and drive each project to completion, so leadership can stay focused on running the business.

**Your projects will have range.** You might lead tax-season readiness planning, run the integration plan for an acquired practice, build a hiring plan, or manage a vendor transition. You won't be an expert in every subject on day one, and that's expected. But you’ll learn fast and inspire confidence as you do. We want someone who can take an unfamiliar problem, turn it into a clear plan, and see it through, leaving behind a documented process so the next iteration is smooth and fast.

**What You'll Do**

* **Plan.** Turn leadership priorities into written project plans with scope, owners, milestones, budgets, and risk assessments. Examples include work-back plans for tax-season readiness, hiring plans, and roadmaps for integrating acquisitions.
* **Track.** Keep every project on a visible schedule, report status to leadership, flag risks early, and push for decisions when a project stalls.
* **Facilitate.** Prepare agendas and pre-reads, capture decisions and action items, and follow up until they're done.
* **Scope.** Find where the practice is stretched: capacity, staffing, systems, workflow, and client experience. Gather data, talk to the team, and turn what you learn into a recommended project with a clear plan.
* **Collaborate.** Partner with the practice managers to unblock projects and turn one-off fixes into documented, repeatable processes.
* **Lead.** Examples include acquisition diligence and integration, vendor selection and contracts, licensing and registrations, and developing policies and procedures.

**What Success Looks Like**

* **First 30 days:** You've gotten to know the team, the systems, and what's in flight. You've built one tracked list of active projects and moved stalled work forward.
* **First 90 days:** You run work on your own from plan to completion, and the team comes to you to get things unstuck.
* **First 6 months:** You own the practice's project portfolio, you've written processes for recurring work, and you've led at least one major planning effort from start to finish, such as tax-season readiness or an acquisition integration.

  
**Requirements**

The ideal candidate will be:

* **Driven.** You don’t wait to be told the next step, and you’re uncomfortable leaving loose ends.
* **Organized.** You keep many threads moving at once without dropping any, and people trust your notes, trackers, and follow-ups.
* **Drawn to the unfamiliar.** “I’ve never done that” makes you curious, not nervous. You learn fast and ask good questions.
* **Resourceful.** You know how to find the right person, document, or answer, and you’re comfortable picking up the phone.
* **A clear communicator.** You write tight summaries and give straight answers, including when the news is bad.
* **Discreet.** You’ll see confidential deal, client, and company information, and you handle it carefully.

### **Core qualifications**

* 3–7 years in a fast-paced role such as operations, consulting, banking, Big 4 -> startup, or a professional services firm.
* A track record of owning messy, ambiguous projects from start to finish.
* Strong analytical skills and comfort using AI tools in day-to-day work.

### **Helpful additions**

* Experience at a CPA, tax, or accounting firm.
* Exposure to M&A, due diligence, or post-acquisition integration.
* Experience with business insurance, vendor management, or HR operations.

With 45 years of experience, we view housing as a fundamental human right and understand that solving homelessness requires a collaborative effort.

The position reports to the Program Manager.

Provide comprehensive case management services. This may include:

Initial eligibility verification and enrollment

Ongoing needs and status assessments

Budgeting

Administration of financial assistance

Information and referral

Crisis de-escalation

Safety planning, risk assessment, and mandated reporting

Employment and benefits assistance

Advocacy

Other direct service provision

Meet with participants at a frequency and location determined by their needs.

Engage in the consistent application of evidence-based practices.

Support internal program support specialist activities as needed. This may include:

Street-based or community outreach efforts

Landlord engagement

Workshop coordination

Achieve identified program and position deliverables.

Adhere to task completion deadlines.
